scenario: Adult with three days of fever, dry cough and sore throat; likely viral infection.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Good morning, please come and sit down. What brings you in today?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Good morning doctor. I have fever and a dry cough, and my throat is sore also.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Okay. Since when have you had this?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Um, two days, no, three days. It started on Sunday evening, I think.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any chest pain or any trouble breathing?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No, no chest pain. And no breathing trouble also, just the cough.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Have you taken anything for the fever so far?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Yes, I took a crocin last night, one tablet. It came down for a few hours and then it came back.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Do you have any allergy to any medicine?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No, no known drug allergies.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Good. Let me check you. Your temperature is 38.2, so you do have a fever. Pulse is 92 and oxygen is 98.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Sorry I was late, doctor. The traffic outside was terrible, I was stuck for forty minutes.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Ha, that road is always like that. Now open your mouth please. Your throat looks a little red. I will listen to your chest now. The chest is clear on both sides.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor, I am a bit worried it could be something serious, like covid or typhoid.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: I think this is most likely a viral infection, and it is very common at this time of year.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay. So what should I take?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Take paracetamol 500 milligrams, one tablet three times a day, only when you feel feverish. I will also give you cetirizine 10 milligrams at night for the throat and the cough.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Do I need any tests today?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Not today. If the fever is still there after three days, we will do a blood test and a chest x-ray.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: And what about food and all that?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Rest at home, drink plenty of warm fluids, and gargle with warm salt water two or three times a day.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Can I go to the office tomorrow?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Better to stay at home for two days. Come back and see me in five days if you are not better, or earlier if the fever goes up.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay doctor, thank you.

gold.key: worried it could be something serious
stay at home for two days
come back and see me in five days

notes: Self-correction in turn 3 (two days, no, three days): the gold duration is the corrected value. Traffic small talk in turns 11 and 12 (first sentence) is deliberately unlabelled. Covid or typhoid in turn 13 is part of the patient's worry, not a clinician assessment. The patient takes crocin (a paracetamol brand) while the doctor prescribes paracetamol and, in addition, cetirizine. This is the consultation where red flags (chest pain, breathing trouble) are explicitly denied.
